statements.text: Space is not a primitive of the principle. It enters as sparse, short-range coupling, which makes distant states conditionally independent and so lets things be told apart, nested at higher spatiotemporal scales.
statements.scope: This repository reads the answer from the sources. They do not pose the question directly.

sources.quote: if the coupling among an ensemble of dynamical systems is mediated by short-range forces, then the states of remote systems must be conditionally independent.
The ensuing statistical independencies, mediated by Markov blankets, speak to a recursive composition of ensembles (of things) at increasingly higher spatiotemporal scales.
